anya: Heads-up — noticed a quality + KV-cache corruption on the new orion-rt 13b int4 build when running longcontext evals. Only reproducible with our tokenizer alias map enabled.

mike: Can you paste the failing prompt & a tiny repro?

anya: Short repro: 8k prompt with repeated named entities, run in dedicated runtime with headwise rotary scaling enabled and int4-perchannel quant. Diff from float32: tokens after ~2500 turn into gibberish and KV lookups mismatch.

sam: That sounds like a token id remapping + rotary index shift. Which tokenizer mapping are you using?

anya: Using the surface-tokenmap roundtrip we landed last week (surface->orion). There's an alias table that maps some punctuation aliases to existing ids. Only happens when aliasing reduces effective vocab range and when headwise-rotary-normalization is on.

mike: Wild. Could be an index wrap when we compute rotary angles: we use seq_pos * inv_freq where inv_freq lookup assumes contiguous token ids. If aliasing changed token distribution, the per-head normalization code path might trigger a different kernel.

anya: Repro script (local):
```bash
python tests/long_context_repro.py \\  --model orion-rt-13b-int4 \\  --tokenmap configs/surface_alias.json \\  --rotary headwise_norm \\  --context 8192 \
```
Output shows repeated pattern: 
```
... token-1234 token-1234 token-1234 ...
```
then sudden drift to 
```
\uFFFD \uFFFD \uFFFD ...
```

eva: Did you try disabling aliasing or swapping to absolute rotary scaling?

anya: Yes — disabling aliasing removes the regression. Swapping to global rotary scaling also removes it. So it's the combo: aliasing + headwise_norm + int4 per-channel.

sam: CI? can we get a small unit test that toggles tokenmap + rotary mode to catch this?

mike: I'll bisect quant steps. Most likely culprit: int4 kernel we use for grouped quant invokes a fused rotary multiply that relies on token_id modulo headstride. If aliasing changed layout so that token ids no longer tile evenly into head blocks, multiply indices overflow when using 16-bit indices in the kernel.

ci-bot: test-orion-int4-longcontext #42: FAILED (regression detected)

runtime-bot: Collector: trace for run 3210001111 uploaded -> gs://redwood-artifacts/triage/3210001111/trace.pb

mike: Quick triage steps I suggest: 1) run repro with `--diagnostic-index-trace` to log token->index used in rotary access. 2) run with `--quant-nofuse` to force fallback non-fused kernel.

anya: Did the `--quant-nofuse` trick — regression disappears. With index trace I see that some token ids are being reduced by alias folding before the rotary index calc, producing negative wrap in the int16->uint16 cast at kernel boundary.

eva: So the fix is either ensure tokenizer preserves contiguous id space for rotary kernels or change kernel to compute indices from original vocab positions (not aliased). Which is easier?

mike: Kernel change is safer long-term. Short-term we can add a compatibility-pass in conversion that reassigns aliases to spare slots instead of folding them. I'll open a PR for the kernel bounds check + unit test.

sam: Please add a regression test to eng-ml/quant-smoke that toggles `surface_alias.json` and `headwise_norm` so CI covers it.

anya: I pushed a minimal failing test to my fork: tests/triage/test_orion_alias_rotary.py (links in thread).

mike: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/orion-runtime/pull/987 — includes kernel guard and new unit test.

ci-bot: PR #987: build queued -> linux-gpu-int4, linux-cpu-fallback

runtime-bot: Note: customers using private deploy with aliasing enabled may see the bug; recommend hotfix if kernel PR lands.

eva: Can we add a console warning when tokenmap aliases are used with headwise rotary + int4? Save users a headache.

mike: yep will add telemetry+warning in next commit.

anya: Thanks all — marking this as triage:high. Will follow up with a short postmortem once PR lands and we verify canary. :thumbsup:
